title: How a blog stores its posts
subtitle: Five tables, and the lines between them

scenes.title: Blog data
scenes.narration: A small blog keeps its writing in five tables. Here is what each one holds, and how they point at each other.

steps.say: Each post has one author, and one author can write many posts.
A post with no publish date is still a draft, so nobody else sees it.
A comment belongs to one post and one user, so it points at both.
Posts and tags meet in a small table in the middle. Each row says this post has this tag, so a post can have many tags and a tag many posts.

scenes.title: Posts tagged postgres
scenes.narration: To find every published post with a tag, the query walks the same lines.

entries.command: select p.title, u.name from posts p join users u on u.id = p.author_id join post_tags pt on pt.post_id = p.id join tags t on t.id = pt.tag_id where t.slug = 'postgres' and p.published_at is not null;
entries.output:
title          |  name
-------------------------+--------
 Indexes you forgot      | Ana
 Why vacuum runs at 3 am | Ravi
(2 rows)

steps.say: It joins posts to their authors, then through the middle table to the tags, and keeps only published posts.
Two posts come back, each with its author.
